'''Swearing''' occurs quite often in the books in both someone saying a swear word and someone thinking one. '''Insults''' also occur just as often.

==Popular Swear Words==
*'''Bloody''' - Is a swear word by itself, "bloody" is also used to enhance or illustrate anger or annoyance (e.g. "blood and bloody ashes" [See blood and ashes], "Bloody women!", "Bloody fools!").
*'''Flaming''' - Is a swear word by itself, "flaming" is also used to preface to another word to show potent expression of anger or annoyance (e.g. "Flaming [[Aes Sedai]]").
*'''Blasted''' - A swear word used in conjunction with another word, similar in usage to "damned" (e.g. "Blasted [[Dragon Reborn]]").
*'''Light''' - Used when astonished (e.g. "Light help us") or an exclamation (e.g. "Light!").
*'''Burn (me, you, other person/group/object)''' - Similar use as damn (e.g. "Damn you", "Burn you") commonly used in response to some upsetting news (e.g. "Burn my bones").

==Insults, Curses, and Vulgar Phrases==
*'''Blood and ashes''' - Expresses anger, disgust, another negative emotion. Commonly intensified by using bloody ("blood and bloody ashes").
*'''Bloody ox of a thimble-brained man'''{{ref/book|4|17}} - Combination of insults and swears meaning a big man with a small brain; another way of calling someone an idiot.
*'''Bilge stone'''{{ref/book|7|39}} - [[Sea Folk]] insult, referring to the waste on board a ship.
*'''Boneheaded'''{{ref/book|3|6}} - Idiotic.
*'''Bull-goose fool''' - A reckless idiot ("twice he had stepped through a ''ter'angreal'' like a bull-goose fool,"{{ref/book|6|5}} "still smiling like a bull-goose fool,"{{ref/book|10|29}} "a pure bull-goose fool"{{ref/book|8|21}}{{ref/book|9|22}}).
*'''Chit''' - Derogatory term for girl, used like 'bitch' or 'twit' ("a lazy chit,"{{ref/book|2|24}} "you ill-tempered little chit,"{{ref/book|5|47}} "if she wore dresses and simpered at him like a brainless chit,"{{ref/book|4|47}} etc.).
*'''Crackbrain'''{{ref/book|4|30}}{{ref/book|10|15}} - Idiotic or crazy.
*'''Daughter/Son of the sands''' - Extreme Sea Folk insult, usually is followed by violence.{{ref/book|7|39}}
*'''Fish-loving scavenger''' - Sea Folk insult, probably not as "mild" as Elayne imagines.{{ref/book|8|6}}
*'''Goat-kissing''' - Describing someone or something as despicable or annoying (e.g. "Goat-kissing [[myrddraal|Halfman]]",{{ref/book|2|11}} "straight through to the goat-kissing ferry,"{{ref/book|2|10}} or "sisters mingling with those goat-kissing [[Asha'man]]{{ref/book|11|Prologue}}).
*'''Goat-spawned toad'''{{ref/book|7|17}} - Generally berating insult.
*'''Goose-brain'''{{ref/book|4|29}} - Idiot; also ''goose-brained''.{{ref/book|9|5}}
*'''Light-blinded fool''' - A righteous, ignorant, misguided, or stupid person ("If you weren't such a Light blinded fool,"{{ref/book|1|13}} or "Burn me for a bloody Light-blinded fool"{{ref/book|3|52}}) Also ''light-blinded idiot''.{{ref/book|1|Prologue}}
*'''Light-forsaken''' - Something that is desolate or wretched ("Even here in this Light-forsaken corner of the world,"{{ref/book|4|31}} or "Light-forsaken axe! Burn me, I wish I had never seen it!"{{ref/book|3|36}})
*'''Lightskirt'''{{ref/book|9|Prologue}} - A person who is "easy," or a slut.
*'''Lummox''' - An oaf, idiot, or lump of a man; usually with an adjective, such as "addle-brained lummox,"{{ref/book|4|29}} "hairy lummox"{{ref/book|4|14}} (one of [[Faile]]'s insults toward [[Perrin]],) "wool-headed lummox,"{{ref/book|2|8}}{{ref/book|3|26}}, or simply "great lummox."{{ref/book|2|48}}
*'''Milk-faced''' - Descriptive of a pretty woman, implying she uses her beauty to tempt men ("He wants a milk-faced vixen who runs about half-naked,"{{ref/book|4|14}} "that milk-faced chit"{{ref/book|3|54}}).
*'''Milk-hearted''' - Cowardly, weak, or timid;{{ref/book|4|50}} sometimes used by [[Aiel]] to describe [[wetlander]]s.{{ref/book|5|5}}{{ref/book|8|1}}
*'''Mule''' - Someone who is stubborn is often compared to a mule ("Stubborn as a cross-eyed mule,"{{ref/book|6|Prologue}} "surlier than a mule with four stone-bruised hooves,"{{ref/book|4|50}} or "mule-headed"{{ref/book|4|53}}).
*'''Mother's milk in a cup''' - Expression of disgust, anger; an obscenity considered particularly vulgar.{{ref/book|9|Prologue}}{{ref/book|10|14}}
*'''Muscle-brained cretin'''{{ref/book|4|17}} - Big, stupid man or one who thinks with his muscles.
*'''Peace!''' - [[Shienaran]] exclamation of surprise or used like "gosh" ("Peace, but it is good to see you"{{ref/book|1|46}}).
*'''Sheep swallop''' - As in, "Oh sheep swallop! Sheep swallop and bloody buttered onions!"{{ref/book|7|38}} Meaning unknown beyond being impressively foul language.
*'''[[Silverpike]]''' - [[Tairen]] expression meaning a swarm of small troubles that together create one big one, can mean persistent, immediate trouble ("[[Samara]]'s a school of silverpike around a chunk of bloody meat"{{ref/book|5|47}}).
*'''Summer ham'''{{ref/book|8|1}} - Coarse and slightly obscure insult.
*'''Thieving fisher-bird''' - [[Tairen]] expression for a sneaky thief ("And burn the thieving fisher-bird,"{{ref/book|3|12}} "had her flapping like a fisher-bird whose catch had been stolen,"{{ref/book|4|47}} "a temper in you like a fisher-bird with a bone in its throat,"{{ref/book|2|18}} "that fool girl has less brains than a fisher-bird"{{ref/book|10|30}}).
*'''Treekillers''' - [[Aiel]] epithet for [[Cairhienin]].
*'''Witches/[[Tar Valon]] witches'''{{ref/book|1|30}} - Epithet used to refer to [[Aes Sedai]], especially common among [[Whitecloaks]].{{ref/book|6|9}}{{ref/book|7|Prologue}}
*'''Wooden-headed buffoon'''{{ref/book|4|14}} - An idiot.
*'''Woolhead''' - A pejorative term used by or about [[Two Rivers]] folk, connoting one who stubbornly denies the obvious or the truth.{{ref|{{twotc}}, woolhead}}.  A common insult used extensively,{{ref/book|1|2}}{{ref/book|2|17}}{{ref/book|6|41}}{{ref/book|8|29}}{{ref/book|9|Prologue}}{{ref/book|9|11}}{{ref/book|9|22}}{{ref/book|9|32}}{{ref/book|10|26}}{{ref/book|11|11}}{{ref/book|11|27}}{{ref/book|11|29}} ''wool-headed'' used just as frequently, often as a "wool-headed fool"{{ref/book|5|2}}{{ref/book|5|54}} {{ref/book|6|10}}{{ref/book|1|27}} or "wool-headed idiot,"{{ref/book|1|35}}{{ref/book|2|12}}{{ref/book|2|24}}{{ref/book|2|38}}{{ref/book|2|39}}{{ref/book|8|27}} referring to an idiot mistake{{ref/book|4|49}}{{ref/book|6|29}} or just a "wool-headed man."{{ref/book|2|23}}{{ref/book|5|55}}

==Obsolete Curses==
*'''Tsag''' - An obscenity uttered by Sammael, possibly from the [[Old Tongue]].{{ref/book|6|6}}
*'''Bajad drovja''' - Another curse from the lips of Sammael, presumably from the [[Age of Legends]].{{ref/book|6|6}}
*'''kjasic ''' - An expletive spoken by Sammael used as an adjective: "in the this ''kjasic'' flyspeck of a city!"{{ref/book|7|15}}
